notes: B3 — the brand's Home tab, and the last of the eight chunks. Drawn last on purpose: Home is a summary of everything else.
the_real_find_is_a_sentence: ⚠️ BrandHomeScreen still tells him to open a laptop. It carries a card reading 'Open web dashboard · Full campaign management + analytics', and its empty state — the FIRST thing a brand with no campaigns ever reads — says 'Create campaigns from the web dashboard'. Stage 2 brought campaign creation to the phone and this screen was never told. A screen nobody re-read after the feature it described was replaced.
home_must_stay_a_summary: Home answers one question: what needs me. Everything else on it is a way into a tab that already exists. The moment Home holds work of its own, two screens begin disagreeing about the same count — the exact fault the six-step ladder was built to end.
changes: Home: needs-you first and itemised; BOTH wallets (to spend, from sales); what is running; the laptop card deleted; the empty state starts a campaign instead of sending him away.
Needs-you: gains 'countered your terms', and a 'waiting on someone else' group so the badge only ever counts things he can act on while the rest stays visible.
Notifications: five new kinds — countered terms, wants a different day, address sent, shop post approved, money from a sale. Each opens the exact screen it is about, not the tab it lives in.
NEW: a first-run screen. Three things to do, and it says plainly that adding products is still web work — the honest answer rather than pretending everything is on the phone.
the_diary_is_kept_and_is_right: BrandDiaryScreen is 18 lines and they are the right 18 — it renders the SAME component the creator reads, wired to the brand's calls. Building it twice is how two sides end up telling different stories about one negotiation.

release.deploy_class: deploy-inert — mockups and specification only, no code
